title: SPARK CSEC Mathematics - Paper 02 Practice Paper C
instructions: This paper consists of THREE sections: I, II and III.
Section I has THREE questions; Section II has THREE questions and Section III has THREE questions.
Numerical answers that are non-exact should be given correct to 3 significant figures or 1 decimal place for angles in degrees, unless a different level of accuracy is specified in the question.
All working MUST be clearly shown.
A table of formulae is provided.

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
Mrs Cadogan buys rice from a wholesaler in bags of 10 kg. The price is $80.00 per bag, and a discount of 10% is given on an order of 20 bags or more. Mrs Cadogan orders 25 bags.

Calculate the TOTAL amount that Mrs Cadogan pays for the 25 bags.
parts.solution: Before the discount the 25 bags cost 25 x $80.00 = $2 000.00. The discount is 10% of $2 000.00 = $200.00, so Mrs Cadogan pays $2 000.00 - $200.00 = $1 800.00.

criteria.description: finding 10% of $2 000.00
the total amount paid

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: Mrs Cadogan sells all 25 bags in her shop at $90.00 per bag. Calculate her percentage profit.
parts.solution: She receives 25 x $90.00 = $2 250.00, so her profit is $2 250.00 - $1 800.00 = $450.00. Her percentage profit is (450.00/1800.00) x 100 = 25%.

criteria.description: expressing the profit as a percentage of the cost price
the percentage profit

questions.stem: Shanice arranges dots in triangular patterns. Pattern 1 is a single dot. Pattern 2 has a row of 2 dots below the single dot. Pattern 3 has a row of 3 dots below Pattern 2, and the pattern continues, each new row having one more dot than the row above it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the number of dots in each pattern. Some rows have not been included.

Study the pattern of numbers in each row of the table. Complete the table by filling in the missing information.
parts.solution: Each pattern adds a row of n dots, so Pattern n has 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n dots, which is n(n + 1)/2. Pattern 4 has 4(5)/2 = 10, Pattern 5 has 5(6)/2 = 15 and Pattern 8 has 8(9)/2 = 36.

dn.description: dots in Pattern n, in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt: A pattern in this sequence has 78 dots. Determine the number of rows in that pattern.
parts.solution: n(n + 1)/2 = 78 gives n(n + 1) = 156. Since 12 x 13 = 156, the pattern has 12 rows.

criteria.description: forms n(n + 1) = 156
the number of rows

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: At a meeting, each of n people shakes hands once with every other person. Write a formula in terms of n for the total number of handshakes.
parts.solution: Each of the n people shakes hands with the other n - 1 people, and each handshake is counted twice, so the total is n(n - 1)/2.

criteria.description: the formula in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
A farmer sells crates of tomatoes and crates of cucumbers at two markets. On one Saturday he sold 24 crates of tomatoes and 36 crates of cucumbers at Market A, and 30 crates of tomatoes and 18 crates of cucumbers at Market B.

Write a 2 x 2 matrix, T, to represent this information, using the rows for Market A and Market B and the columns for tomatoes and cucumbers.
parts.solution: The two rows are Market A and Market B and the two columns are tomatoes and cucumbers, so T = [[24, 36], [30, 18]].

criteria.description: the matrix T

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt:
A crate of tomatoes sells for $45.00 and a crate of cucumbers sells for $25.00.

Write a 2 x 1 matrix, P, to represent the selling price, in dollars, of one crate of tomatoes and of one crate of cucumbers.
parts.solution: P is a column matrix with one entry for each of the two items, in the same order as the columns of T, so P = [[45], [25]].

criteria.description: the matrix P, with the correct rows and columns

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the matrix product TP.
parts.solution: TP = [[24, 36], [30, 18]][[45], [25]]. Multiplying the first row of T by the column P gives (24 x 45) + (36 x 25) = 1080 + 900 = 1980, and the second row gives (30 x 45) + (18 x 25) = 1350 + 450 = 1800. So TP = [[1980], [1800]].

criteria.description: multiplying each row of T by the column P
the matrix product TP

parts.label: (b) (iv)
parts.prompt: What does the matrix product TP represent?
parts.answer: TP represents the total amount of money, in dollars, received at each market: $1980 at Market A and $1800 at Market B
parts.solution: The first row of TP is (24 x 15) + (36 x 9), the value of the tomatoes added to the value of the cucumbers sold at Market A. So TP represents the total amount of money received at each market: $1980 at Market A and $1800 at Market B.

rubric.description: says that TP gives the total amount received at each market

questions.topic: Geometric construction and trigonometry in right-angled triangles

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
The angle XYZ, of size 120°, is drawn on the construction pad.

Using only a ruler and a pair of compasses, construct the bisector of angle XYZ. Your construction arcs must be clearly shown.
parts.answer: the bisector of angle XYZ drawn from Y, with the arc centred at Y and the two equal arcs from where it cuts YX and YZ left on the page
parts.solution: With centre Y, draw an arc that cuts YX and YZ. From each of those two crossing points, with the same radius, draw an arc so that the two arcs cross each other. Rule the straight line from Y through that crossing point: it is the bisector of angle XYZ. All three arcs must be left on the page - an angle measured with a protractor and halved earns no construction mark.

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Your bisector passes through the point W. State, giving a reason for your answer, the size of angle XYW.
parts.answer: Angle XYW = 60°, because the bisector divides angle XYZ into two equal angles, and half of 120° is 60°
parts.solution: The bisector of an angle divides it into two equal angles. Angle XYZ = 120°, so angle XYW = angle WYZ = 120/2 = 60°.

rubric.description: states 60 degrees and says that the bisector divides angle XYZ into two equal angles

parts.prompt:
The diagram below shows a ladder AC, of length 8.5 m, leaning against a vertical wall BC. The foot of the ladder is on level ground, 4 m from the wall.

State, giving a reason for your answer, the size of angle ABC.
parts.answer: Angle ABC = 90°, because the wall BC is vertical and the ground AB is horizontal, so BC is perpendicular to AB
parts.solution: The wall BC stands vertically and the ground AB is horizontal, so BC is perpendicular to AB. The angle between them, angle ABC, is therefore 90°.

rubric.description: states 90 degrees and says that the wall is perpendicular to the ground

parts.prompt: Calculate the length of BC, the height that the ladder reaches up the wall.
parts.solution: Angle ABC = 90°, so by Pythagoras' theorem BC^2 = AC^2 - AB^2 = 8.5^2 - 4^2 = 72.25 - 16 = 56.25. So BC = sqrt(56.25) = 7.5 m.

questions.topic: Coordinate geometry, functions and the graph of a quadratic

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
The line DE passes through the points D(-4, -1) and E(2, 3).

Determine the gradient of the line DE.
parts.solution: The gradient of DE is m = (3 - (-1))/(2 - (-4)), that is 4/6, which simplifies to 2/3.

criteria.description: the difference in y over the difference in x
the gradient of DE, in its lowest terms

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Determine the equation of the line which passes through E and which is perpendicular to the line DE.
parts.solution: The gradient of DE is 2/3, so the gradient of a line perpendicular to DE is -3/2, because the product of the two gradients must be -1. Using y = mx + c with E(2, 3): 3 = (-3/2)(2) + c, so c = 6. The equation of the line is y = -(3/2)x + 6.

criteria.description: the gradient of the perpendicular line
the equation of the perpendicular line

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The functions f and g are defined as

f(x) = 5x + 2   and   g(x) = (x - 1)/(x + 3), x != -3.

Determine the value of gf(3).

criteria.description: evaluating f(3) and substituting it into g
the value of gf(3)

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Derive a simplified expression for g^(-1)(x).
parts.solution: Let y = g(x), so y = (x - 1)/(x + 3). Interchanging x and y gives x = (y - 1)/(y + 3), so x(y + 3) = y - 1. Expanding the left-hand side, xy + 3x = y - 1. Collecting the terms in y on one side gives xy - y = -3x - 1, that is y(x - 1) = -3x - 1. Dividing by x - 1 gives g^(-1)(x) = (3x + 1)/(1 - x).

criteria.description: interchanging x and y and clearing the fraction
collecting the terms in y on one side
the correct inverse

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration of the train during the last 12 seconds.
parts.solution: During the last 12 seconds the speed changes from 6 m/s to 30 m/s, a change of 24 m/s, and it takes 12 seconds. The acceleration is the gradient of that stage of the graph: the change in speed divided by the time taken, which is 2 m/s^2.

the acceleration

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the TOTAL distance travelled by the train during the 22 seconds.
parts.solution: The distance travelled is the area under the speed-time graph. The graph is never at rest while the speed is changing, so that stage is a TRAPEZIUM and not a triangle: the rectangle from 0 s to 10 s has area 6 x 10 = 60; the trapezium from 10 s to 22 s has area 1/2(6 + 30)(12) = 216. The total distance is therefore 276 m.

criteria.description: treats the distance as the area under the graph, taking the sloping stage as a trapezium and not as the triangle underneath it
the total distance
